Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The printed schedule goes to the library desk and the community notice board on September 22.

Our regular broadcast week runs from Monday to Sunday, with a live evening block on Thursday. The transmitter is maintained by the regional service, not by our volunteers, and the service has confirmed our usual hours for October. Jo checked the room calendar and found that the library will close early on October 17 for staff training. That does not change our transmission hours, but it means our volunteers need to leave the building by 8:30 p.m. I have kept the Thursday program in the schedule and asked Jo to confirm which volunteers can pack up before then.

I am asking Tomas to contact the caretaker by September 12 and ask whether those names are on the list. He should report the answer to me, not send a general message to all presenters, since the access information concerns only that Thursday team.

The October schedule has several changes from September, although the weekday morning programs remain in their usual places. I used the same half-hour grid as last month so listeners can compare the printed pages. The new programs and adjustments are these:

1. Monday at 6:00 p.m., “Harbor Voices” replaces the repeat of “Garden Bench.” Jo recorded two interviews with ferry workers for this program, and she has booked the station’s editing room for October 6.
2. Tuesday at 7:30 p.m., the local history desk returns with a live call-in. The history desk asked for a second phone line, but we have not confirmed that equipment is available. I marked the slot as live without promising the extra line.
3. Wednesday at 5:00 p.m., “Small Repairs” moves from 5:30. Its host, Dinesh Rao, requested the earlier time because his evening class begins at 6:15. I made the change after checking that the youth bulletin ends at 4:45.
4. Thursday at 8:00 p.m., the volunteer music hour stays in place. The library’s early closure on October 17 applies to the people in the building, not to the transmitter schedule.
5. Sunday at 11:00 a.m., the poetry reading is listed as a repeat. The recording is from September 28, and the poet has agreed to a repeat on air, but the web page still needs the correct title.

I am asking Tomas to check the web page title against the recording label and send me the exact wording by September 15. The label reads “Rooms With Open Windows,” while the draft page says “Room With Open Windows.” I have not changed the page because I cannot tell whether the label is a final title or a working name. Tomas should ask Jo, who received the recording, rather than contact the poet directly. Jo said, “I wrote down the title as it was given to me, but I didn’t see the final program card.” That is why I want the wording checked before the page is updated.

There are two other practical matters for the schedule. The equipment grant covers replacement headphones and one portable recorder, but it does not cover presenter travel. Jo submitted the headphone receipt on September 3 and put the recorder request in a separate note; the grant office has acknowledged receiving both items but has not said whether the recorder will be funded. I have listed the field interview as recorded in the studio, not on location, so the printed schedule does not imply that we have a portable recorder. If the grant office confirms the recorder before September 18, I can revise the web description to say the interview was recorded at the ferry terminal. If there is no confirmation by then, the schedule and description should stay as they are.

The station also received three listener suggestions for October. One person asked for more local weather information, another asked for a monthly repair program, and a third asked that we repeat the public meeting recordings sooner. I gave the suggestions to Jo because she coordinates the volunteer discussion, and she has not promised any of those changes. She proposed that we test a short weather note in the Monday news slot, but that is only a proposal for the November schedule. I have not added it to October. The repair program is already listed on Wednesday, and the public meeting recordings depend on when the council sends us an approved file.

For the printed page, I am keeping program titles in quotation marks and using the same contact number that appears on the station door. The number is for the studio desk during staffed hours; it is not a call-in line for every program. The Tuesday history desk can take calls only if the second line is available, so I have left its phone number off the public schedule for now. Jo has checked the weekday times against the presenter roster and found no overlap, but the Sunday repeat still needs the correct title.
